prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H]1c2ccccc2OC[C@H]1O
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL243

Assay A:
  Description: In vitro inhibition of HIV-1 protease
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibitory activity against HIV-1 protease.
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw:
```json
{"call": "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": 0.9,
 "error_class": "assay_method",
 "reason": "The assay descriptions lack critical experimental details, such as substrate and enzyme concentrations, which strongly influence HIV-1 protease IC50 values and make it impossible to determine commensurability."}
```

parsed.reason: The assay descriptions lack critical experimental details, such as substrate and enzyme concentrations, which strongly influence HIV-1 protease IC50 values and make it impossible to determine commensurability.
